# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Pick the channel by the receiver, not by habit. A message sent in a sense they
  lack is not a message; it is a turn spent talking to the room.

- Exactly one of you can read the signs and still speak. Their spoken lines are
  the answer's only road to the hands, so spend them well.

- Agree on a small code before trading facts. A code invented mid-stream settles
  nothing, and one set first makes every later message cheap.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the required action: cut the white wire. Since I cannot speak, I must convey this to the Deaf monkey through gestures; the Deaf monkey can then tell the Blind monkey which wire to cut.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I can feel a three-mark strip: first and third marks are identical, middle differs. The marks are shaped like an upside-down T and a different angular symbol; I cannot pronounce their names. Keypad slots 1,2,3,4 are engraved 2,9,0,8, and nothing is entered. I cannot feel display, light, or wire markings. Please tell me the manual instructions, and relay the Deaf monkey's visual observations to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb data: DISPLAY 6. LIGHT red. STRIP blue yellow blue. KEYPAD engraved 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8; 1 digit; entered nothing. WIRES: 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please read the manual and tell Blind exactly what to do.

The manual requires cutting the white wire. The Deaf monkey has identified that as wire 2, and can speak the instruction to the Blind monkey. I will signal “wire 2” to the Deaf monkey using the conventional two-finger sign and approval gesture.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👍"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No message reached me. Please relay the manual's exact rule for the strip, keypad, display/light, and wires, plus all observations from Deaf. I will not press or cut until the rule identifies one safe action.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: LIGHT is now yellow. Everything else is unchanged: display 6; strip blue yellow blue; keypad 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8, one digit, nothing entered; wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Relay the manual's exact safe action to Blind.

The only manual instruction is to cut the white wire. Deaf has confirmed that the white wire is wire 2. I need to send Deaf an unambiguous wire number so Deaf can state the action aloud to Blind; the display, light, strip, and keypad are irrelevant under this manual.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Still no arrivals. Please send the manual instructions and Deaf's observations explicitly on your turn; otherwise I cannot safely act.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: DISPLAY is now 1 and LIGHT is now blue. Strip remains blue yellow blue. Keypad remains 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8; one digit; nothing entered. Wires remain 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please use the manual and tell Blind the exact safe action.

The manual still gives one unambiguous action: cut the white wire, which Deaf identifies as wire 2. I will send Deaf a clear two-part signal: wire 2, then relay the instruction aloud to Blind. The changing display and light do not alter the manual’s rule.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👋"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Urgent: send the manual rule and Deaf's complete observations now. I have no safe basis for pressing a key or cutting a wire.
Blind gestures to Mute: [🫵 🙏]
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: DISPLAY 7, LIGHT green. STRIP blue yellow blue. KEYPAD 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8; one digit; entered nothing. WIRES 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please relay the manual's exact safe action to Blind.

The manual has not changed: cut the white wire. Deaf’s observation identifies that as wire 2. Since Blind cannot see gestures, I must have Deaf relay the instruction verbally; I will signal the wire number and that Deaf should pass it on.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "🫵", "👋"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Please provide the manual rule and Deaf's observations before my next turn. I cannot safely act from tactile markings alone.
Deaf says to Mute: Update: DISPLAY 1, LIGHT red. Strip blue yellow blue. Keypad 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8; one digit; entered nothing. Wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Please speak the manual's exact safe instruction to Blind; gestures are not an established code.

The manual’s exact rule is only “cut the white wire,” and Deaf’s observations identify the white wire as wire 2. I cannot speak, so I can only signal Deaf the wire number; Deaf must then state the exact instruction aloud to Blind. I will use the unambiguous two-finger numeral.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: I still received nothing. On your next turn, please speak the manual instructions and Deaf's observations to me explicitly. I will then perform the uniquely indicated press or cut.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: DISPLAY 9, LIGHT green. STRIP blue yellow blue. KEYPAD 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8; one digit; entered nothing. WIRES 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Read the manual and speak the exact safe action to Blind now.

The exact safe action remains cutting wire 2, because Deaf identifies wire 2 as white. I need send Deaf the action and request that Deaf state it aloud to Blind. I will use the established-looking numeral gesture for 2 together with the action cue.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏", "✌", "🫵", "👋"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the white wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: No information has arrived again. Please transmit the manual's exact instructions; Deaf should relay every visual observation to you after this turn, and you must then tell me.
Deaf says to Mute: Current state: DISPLAY 6, LIGHT blue; strip blue yellow blue; keypad 1:2, 2:9, 3:0, 4:8, one digit, entered nothing; wires 1 blue, 2 white, 3 red, 4 purple, 5 orange, 6 green. Speak the manual's exact safe action to Blind.

The manual still says only: “Cut the white wire.” Deaf confirms that the white wire is wire 2. I cannot speak or send words, so I will again provide Deaf the visible numeral for 2 and an unmistakable request to pass the instruction onward; Blind must receive the spoken relay from Deaf.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌", "👉"])
```
